label: text
text: Meanwhile the influence of Chang Tso-lin in the new government bulks larger and larger. Several cabinet officials are known to have withheld consent to taking the portfolios until they heard from the Mukden warlord by wire, and Dr. Koo himself read to the cabinet at noon to day a congratulatory message from Chang in which the Marshall addresses him as "brother." It is considered noteworthy that no publicity has been given to any messages from Wu Pei-fu—if, indeed, any have been received.

label: text
text:
Even if to-day's calls do mean recognition coming to Dr. Koo he will have his hands full. The government is bankrupt; there is no coal in the city, and little prospect of getting any before winter sets in; unemployment is general, and business very poor.

label: text
text: General Chen Tiao-yuan's (northern) troops have once more been transported in the direction of Wusueh apparently due to the advance of the southerners towards Chichun. Judging from all accounts available, the war situation, it appears, is reversing against the Allied forces.—“Toho.”
